blocks.text: Sulfur has two oxides, sulfur dioxide and sulfur trioxide, collectively SOx. They are emitted primarily by burning coal and oil. When SOx combines with water vapour it causes acid rain, which damages ecosystems; SO2 is the major source of acid deposition in the air.

blocks.prompt: Why is SO2 rather than SO3 called the major source of acid deposition?
blocks.explanation: Combustion releases sulfur mainly as SO2; only part of it is oxidised in the air to SO3. The SO2 dissolves in moisture as sulfurous acid and is slowly oxidised to sulfuric acid, so the quantity of acid deposited depends chiefly on the SO2 emitted.

items: SOx = SO2 + SO3, from burning coal and oil; with water vapour gives acid rain; SO2 is the major source of acid deposition.
